newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore jails tanker captain for oil spill.
newsitem.headline: Singapore jails tanker captain for oil spill.

text.p: Singapore handed out record penalties on Friday for a harbour oil spill, jailing the tanker captain for nearly six months and imposing large fines, the government's Maritime and Port Authority (MPA) said.

It said in a statement that Brendon Allan Monteiro, the 40-year-old Indian captain of the Song San, was sentenced to a total of 13-1/2 months in jail out of which he would serve 5-1/2 months because some of the sentences were to run concurrently.
A Singapore court also fined Monteiro Singapore $400,000 (US$286,000) for the spill last August which polluted "extensive areas of Singapore's waters and beaches", the MPA statement said.
MPA said they don't know if captain and chief officers were held in custody or out on bail and legal authorties were not immediately contactable.
It said this was the first time a seaman had been jailed in Singapore for marine pollution and not maintaining his ship's oil record book.
Monteiro was found guilty of marine pollution, not maintaining the tanker's oil record book and giving false or misleading statements to investigators, the MPA said.
Pashupati Nath, 35, chief officer of the 230,000 DWT tanker registered in Singapore, was jailed for six weeks for giving "false or misleading" statements to investigators, the MPA said.
It did not give his nationality.
It said the court also fined owners Dong Sheng Tankers Pte Ltd S$450,000 and agents Ocean Tankers Pte Ltd S$400,000. ($1 = S$1.4)
